results.term_definition:
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun in the Solar System. It is a rocky, terrestrial planet with a radius of a little under 3400 kilometers (km), just over one half of the Earth's radius. Mars has a very thin atmosphere, a large canyon system, and the tallest mountain in the Solar System: an extinct volcano called Olympus Mons. It is thought to have hosted liquid water earlier in its existence.

Its typical distance from the Sun is about 228 million km or 1.52 astronomical units (Earth–Sun distances). It takes 687 days to complete one orbit of the Sun. Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.

It is named after the Roman god of war. It is often called the "red planet" due to its reddish rusty color. Scientists have sent many landers to Mars over the years to study its composition and atmosphere.
